findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never upgraded with the Clients schema
findings.body: `init` returns as soon as the realm already has an admin-permissions client. Realms which enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore retain only the old Users resource/scopes and never receive the Clients all-resource or the new configure/map-role scopes. Creating a Client permission in such a realm will fail when `getOrCreateResource` cannot find the required scope, and all-clients evaluation cannot work. The initialization/migration path must add missing schema scopes and resource-type resources to an existing admin-permissions client rather than returning unconditionally.

findings.title: Per-client resources are created without their Clients type
findings.body: Resources created for an individual client are assigned scopes but never assigned `resourceType` (for example via `resource.setType(resourceType)`). `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission` later uses `resourceStore.findByType(..., "Clients", ...)` to determine which clients the caller may access, so it will not discover any of these untyped per-client resources. Consequently a user granted view/manage for one client can be omitted from filtered client listings/access calculations despite the direct permission evaluating successfully.

findings.title: Role-mapping checks discard the manage-clients authorization path
findings.body: `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only test their respective fine-grained scope. Unlike the other client operations, they do not allow `MANAGE_CLIENTS` through `canManage(client)`. Thus an administrator with the normal `manage-clients` role (or a V2 manage permission) is denied client-role mapping/composite operations unless separately granted every map scope, which regresses the established meaning of manage-clients and makes existing administrators fail after V2 is enabled.
